entry.title: What do Spider Strings do in Hollow Knight Silksong
entry.summary:
Spider Strings is a creepy-looking item in Hollow Knight Silksong that can be extremely useful as you approach the endgame content.
Spider Strings is a yellow tool in nature that can be purchased directly from a trader. But let's first look at what it does, and whether buying it is worth it.
Table of contents How to get Spider Strings in Hollow Knight Silksong?
How does Spider Strings work in Hollow Knight Silksong?
The function of Spider Strings is apparent from its official in-game description.
Sophisticated Weaver device. Resonates with music played to amplify and enhance a performance. Expands and strengthens the effects of the Needolin."
In simpler terms, it provides a passive boost to the effects of your Needolin. This is exceptionally important for the late-game and endgame activities. Whether you can perfectly time your attacks or rely on wild slashes, empowering your Needolin always has certain benefits.
Let's find out how you can obtain the tool.
Remix by Destructoid via Team Cherry
How to get Spider Strings in Hollow Knight Silksong?
The first task is to complete the Wandering Merchant Wish. You'll need to help a roaming trader who will allow you to get new items in certain Pharloom shops. Next, you'll have to go to the Choral Chambers in the Songclave region.
You'll find Jubilana Merchant there, who offers Spider Strings among many other items. You can obtain the Spider Strings by exchanging 320 Rosaries. However, you'll only find the item after clearing the Wandering Merchant Wish. Until you've cleared the quest, the item won't be added to Jubilana's stock.
Once you have purchased the item, you must equip it from your inventory to activate its effects.

entry.title: Today is PlayStation’s 30th birthday in the US. What’s your G.O.A.T. PS1 game?
entry.summary:
Happy 30th American birthday, PlayStation!
On this day, 30 years ago, the PlayStation was first released in the United States. What followed can only be described as some of the most iconic games and memories that have withstood the test of time to this day.
The PS1 gave us many classic games, and it was the birthplace of franchises that are still dropping bangers to this day, or it continued to expand on series that began before it by elevating things with 3D graphics and more.
Metal Gear Solid. Final Fantasy VII. Resident Evil. Silent Hill. Twisted Metal. Tomb Raider. Ape Escape. Tekken. Crash Bandicoot. Ridge Racer. Chrono Cross. Dino Crisis. Oddworld: Abe's Odyssee. Gran Turismo. Syphon Filter. Castlevania: Symphony of the Night. Need for Speed. Ace Combat. PaRappa the Rapper. Spider-Man. Parasite Eve. Medal of Honor.
Shall I continue? I won't, but you get the picture. A lot of us elder gamers were formed by the PS1 days. I can speak for myself in saying that MGS1, Final Fantasy VIII, and Resident Evil formed a triumvirate of favorite franchises that I still love, look forward to, and play to this very day, 30 years later. But many other memories were formed with several other titles mentioned above, and that's still just scratching the surface.
Now, I pose the question to you, dear reader. What's your G.O.A.T. PS1 game? Which is the game you think of when you hear that iconic start-up sound? Let us know in the poll and comments below in celebration of today's anniversary, and then let's boot up some classics for old time's sake.

entry.title: Where to find the Apostate Key in Hollow Knight Silksong
entry.summary:
The Apostate Key is vital in Hollow Knight Silksong as you are approaching the endgame content, and it's one of the three Slab Keys spread across Pharloom.
Just like the Simple Key, getting the Apostate Key (or the Key of Apostate) will allow you to access more memories. However, you won't have any objective marker pointing you in the right direction.
This guide will help you find this elusive item in Hollow Knight Silksong.
Apostate Key location in Hollow Knight Silksong
There are different ways to reach the Apostate Key, but the road won't be easy. It's filled with monsters and tough terrain. The path I chose for this guide can be accessed from the Bench in Bilewater, and you'll need the Wall Climb, Dash, and the Double Jump abilities. That part shouldn't be a problem since we are discussing the endgame stage.
Screenshot by Destructoid
From the bench, go left and jump onto the next couple of platforms to the next room.
Cross the room with the available platforms, and you'll come across a point where you can either go up or down.
Screenshot by Destructoid
Go up, for which you'll need to be able to Wall Climb and Double Jump. Head up until you can access the next platform and move to the next room.
Use the ledges until you reach the top of the new room, and you'll find a path going left.
As you move forward, keep landing your attacks. There's a monster here. Bait it and force it to rush towards you. Then jump on top of it and keep going left.
Reach the ledge, double jump, dash to reach the next one, and you'll find the Apostate Key there.
Please note that two more Slab keys are scattered throughout Hollow Knight Silksong. All three of them are hard to obtain, and you'll need to unlock all the abilities before you can find them.

entry.title: Our favourite videogame vapourware: No Silksong Allowed Edition
entry.summary: Vapourware! We all say we despise it, but everybody loves thinking about games that spend an eternity in limbo, whether due to chronic mismanagement or simply because the developers feel no need to rush. So many teasers to unravel, so many conspiracies to bake from the most ludicrous of breadcrumbs, so much delicious exasperation to wallow in as yet another year goes by without a new trailer. Hollow Knight: Silksong is no longer vapourware, barring some extreme last-minute drama. Announced in 2019, it will finally launch this Thursday 4th September. entry.title: What can a 34-year-old Sonic level teach us about videogame light?

No videogame fantasy setting will ever disquiet me as much as an empty business park at night under blue and yellow floodlights. A business park, or the access road down the side of a corrugated steel warehouse, where the alcoves cast by the LEDs look like a procession of hooded figures beneath the fixed, unblinking blackness of the sky. I can't actually be present in that scene, mind. I don't belong there. No being does, not even the people who come by day to fill the striped lines with cars or raise the shutters on the loading bays. Instead, I have to be travelling past very fast. Preferably, I will be looking out the window of a train that shows the place for only a few seconds. I will feel as though I've glimpsed another planet's scrolling surface in a mirror. entry.title: Elden Ring Nightreign's evil Deep Of Night mode gets a release date, but some people are already playing it
entry.summary:
Elden Ring Nightreign will get a new rock-hard Expedition mode called Deep of Night on 11th September. "Rock-hard" is a cliché worn to uselessness, of course: to be more specific, this is at least tungsten-carbide-hard, possibly even as hard as stishovite, though the exact degree of toughness is variable.
It's variable because Deep of Night gets statistically harder, the more you win, with a difficulty rating or "depth" that fluctuates based on wins and losses. Enemies are tougher than usual by default, and you can't specify which Nightlord you're hunting, so be prepared for nasty surprises. There are new special Depth Relics, exclusive to this mode, which sadistically bundle together additional buffs and debuffs.

entry.title: Coffee convos, demonic detectives, and cow life simming are part of a pro-Palestine charity bundle coming to Itch.io
entry.summary: A bundle of games aiming to raise money to aid the United Nations' Relief and Works Agency (UNRWA) in their efforts to help Palestinian refugees is set to go on sale via Itch.io next week. Just over 380 games are part of it, including the likes of Coffee Talk, Lucifer Within Us, and a cow life simulator that features an alligator who's really into arson. Organised by Junch and the South East Asian Games for Good initiative, the bundle's dubbed Play for Peace - Games for Palestine. It's taken over 10 months to come together. The result's a 382-game strong bundle that includes a huge variety of creations that contain not a whiff of AI or NFTs. Read more

entry.title: Bioshock successor Judas emerges from hiding as Ken Levine explains how you'll choose the game's final villain
entry.summary: You know when you're friends with three people, then one of them suddenly pulls a Robbie Rotten and morphs into a real villain who terrorises your existence? No? entry.title: Announcing support for World Builder-based games
entry.summary: After many years of development, games made with World Builder are ready for testing. The World Builder creation system was released for the original Macintosh and was extremely popular among developers. As such, we're announcing that over 160 games built on the engine are ready for public testing in ScummVM. Notable games made with World Builder include: Ray's Maze. The game follows Frank Farley, a part-time adventurer, who finds himself in a Maze full of dangerous monsters and deadly traps. The objective of the game is to solve puzzles and escape the maze. Radical Castle. You are given the role of a squire, who must bring back the stolen "Oracle" to the King to escape a fatal punishment. Enchanced Scepters. The first game created using World Builder, and one of the few commercial games made with it. The player must find fire, earth, air, and water scepters and bring them back to the castle. Most games made with WAGE are either freeware or shareware, and for your convenience we've collected all titles with these types into one big downloadable archive. So grab it from our game downloads page, get yourself a daily development build, and start your journey. As always, if you happen to have any issues, please submit the bug reports to our issue tracker. Lastly, contact us if you have some other unrecognised games or a new demo. >
